subject: mathematics
question_text: If A = (1, −2, −1), B = (4, 0, −3), C = (1, 2, −1) and D = (2, −4, −5), then find the distance between the lines AB and CD.

mark_split.label: Build the two lines in r = a + tb form

steps.label: Build the two lines
steps.margin_note: Second mark. A line through two points has the first as its POINT and the difference as its DIRECTION. That is what turns four points into the r = a + tb form the formula needs.

steps.why: The formula from answer 23 needs a point and a direction for each line. Four points give exactly that, once the subtractions are done.
common_mistakes: Using OB as the direction instead of OB − OA.

steps.label: Find a − c
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The i and k terms cancel completely here, leaving a single j term — which makes the dot product below very short.
steps.memory_tip: The i and k terms cancel completely, leaving a single j term — which shortens the dot product.

recall.must_convey: That a − c comes to −4j, with the i and k components cancelling.
accept: a minus c is minus four j, the i and k parts cancel
subtracting gives only a j term, minus four j

steps.why: A and C share their i and k coordinates, so the joining vector points purely along j. Spotting that saves work in the next step.
common_mistakes: Carrying phantom i or k terms through.

steps.label: Find b×d
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Cross the two DIRECTIONS, not the points.
steps.memory_tip: Cross the two DIRECTIONS, not the points.

recall.must_convey: That b×d is computed from the two direction vectors, giving −20i + 10j − 20k.
accept: cross the two directions to get minus twenty i plus ten j minus twenty k
b cross d comes from the direction vectors

steps.why: The cross product is non-zero, which is what confirms the two lines are not parallel — a necessary condition before this formula applies at all.
common_mistakes: Crossing the position vectors instead of the directions.
Sign slip on the j term.

steps.label: Numerator and denominator
steps.margin_note: Fifth mark. Because a − c is only a j term, the dot product picks out just the j component of b×d — one multiplication instead of three.
steps.memory_tip: Because a − c is only a j term, the dot product picks out just the j component of b×d.

recall.must_convey: That the numerator is −40 and |b×d| is 30.
accept: the dot product is minus forty and the magnitude is thirty
minus four times ten gives minus forty, and root nine hundred is thirty
numerator minus forty, denominator thirty

the two pieces are minus forty and thirty

steps.why: A dot product with a single-component vector only ever picks up one term. Recognising that is a real time saving under exam conditions.
common_mistakes: Multiplying all three components of b×d by −4.

steps.label: Divide
steps.margin_note: The last three marks. The modulus makes the −40 positive, and 40/30 cancels to 4/3. Leave it as a fraction — decimals are not expected.
steps.memory_tip: The modulus makes −40 positive, and 40/30 cancels to 4/3. Leave it as a fraction.

recall.must_convey: That the modulus makes it 40/30, which cancels to 4/3 units.
accept: mod of minus forty over thirty is forty over thirty which is four thirds
the distance is four by three units
cancelling gives four over three
forty by thirty equals four by three units
the answer is four thirds

steps.why: The modulus is what makes the sign of the numerator irrelevant — a distance cannot be negative however the subtraction was ordered.
